raw_recipe.headline: Lebanese Lemon Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Tangy, zesty, garlicky lemon and olive oil flavors blend in this dressing that compliments salads which include some type of grilled meat and baked or fried pita chips in the place of croutons. This dressing is best with salads containing grilled chicken, shrimp or fish. It is very tangy but absolutely yummy.
raw_recipe.name: Lebanese Lemon Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper. Stir just before serving.

review.reviewBody: My husband is always chiding me for using too much lemon in some dishes. I was expecting more of the same from him so I made this dressing and served it on the side. My mouth dropped open when he told me that I will be making this dressing anytime I serve salad from now on. This man is a die hard ranch dressing person. This is a huge compliment to the author. I loved the dressing too. Fresh squeezed lemons are a must. DON'T USE BOTTLED LEMON JUICE! FRESH LEMONS ONLY!

I am a Lebanese woman and this is the exact dressing I use for all of my salads. I would like to make two comments. 1. Use BIG cubes of garlic. 2. You can actually make this salad ahead. Make the drsg in large bowl then, add lettuce and veggies on top of drsg. Toss right before serving. Do not toss salad or add drsg until just ready to serve or your salad will get soggy. Enjoy!

I cut the recipe in half & added a few spices, I loved it with the additions: 1/4 Cup lemon, 1/4 Cup olive Oil, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, pepper to taste, 1 teaspoon of thyme, red bell pepper flakes to taste, garlic powder, and fresh minced garlic. In a gallon ziploc plastic bag, Mix dressing, kale, & whatever else you like in salad...then let it sit in the refrigerator for half an hour. Yum!
Very tasty. I used one whole lemon and added a couple tablespoons of Braggs Apple Cider vinegar. Added a touch of honey. Delicious.
Made this with Meyer Lemon, because that is what I had on hand. Just put it all in jar and shook it up rather than whisking, worked fine. So yummy on a salad of green, tomato, tuna and chickpeas! :)
I use this recipe and add 2 green onions and 1 bunch of fresh parsley. Coarse chop all ingredients in a food processor. Serve with crackers and your favorite hummus. Wonderful!

This is the only salad dressing we use. We add french bread cut into 1/2" cubes to the salad. The bread soaks up some of the dressing. We use Romaine lettuce and add grated parmesan cheese and cut-up anchovies. It is simply the best and inexpensive to make.
Love the lemony and garlic taste, so refreshing! But being on Weight Watchers I use 1/4 cup of olive oil and 1/4 cup chicken broth. Saves on fat and calories!
Love it! Did add 1 tsp. Sugar to cut the tang a bit for salad.

for anyone who thinks that this recipe is to tangy or acidic try this take 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, to 3/4 cup mild olive oil or you can cut extra virgin olive oil with veg/canola oil 50/50 with 3-4 cloves garlic and kosher salt and pepper to taste. Most salad dressing have a 3-1 ratio much more pleasant on the palate.

One of the comments notes that it is very lemony and another comment suggests not using bottled lemon juice. 
I am Lebanese and I grew up with this dressing and it is the only dressing I use. If you use fresh lemons, you have to recognize that all lemons are not created equally so you have to temper it if your lemons are especially tart. I also don't use equal parts olive oil. I use far less olive oil than called for. So will fresh garlic and fresh lemons taste better. Sure if the garlic still is fresh and the lemons are just the right tartness. 
But for a really easy way to do it that still tastes fresh and clean - cut up your ingredients, splash them with a lemon juice (Costco has organic lemon juice with no additives) and just about half as much olive olive oil and then GARLIC salt and pepper to taste. The combination garlic salt gives you about the right amount of garlic. 
So would I fix it the easy way for company - no. But I fix it this way and pour it over pre-cut cabbage (cole slaw) or pre-cut salads or precut kale salad sold at Costco for a very quick and easy salad
I used my garlic press and my immersion blender…was absolutely perfect
Love this dressing! It’s so versatile and delicious, I love it on Greek salads and goes great with seafood and poultry!
It's perfect. Made exactly as described, perfect for fattoush.
Yummy on a green salad with marinated shrimp
Only change made is did not add garlic simply because I was out. Very yummy and refreshing.

I have never met a homemade salad that I love, so I have embarked on a mission to explore more dressings/salad recipes, and I started with this. It was pretty good. My hubby enjoyed it too. I drizzled it on cukes from our garden, sweet peppers, tomato, avocado, grilled chicken and feta. I will give it another go with a different mix with the leftovers. Thanks for the recipe!
Wow! this recipe is delicious as is. I opted for a bit less salt. It was enjoyed by many. Thanks!
This tastes like La Marsa dressing. It’s simple and easy to make and tastes delicious!
Just like my favorite Lebanese restaurant, Cafe du Liban. Thank you for sharing this. My whole family loves it! I doubled the recipe and added one packet of Truvia.
